top.title: El Cerrito police expect to make 'multiple arrests' over HS football hazing
top.description: El Cerrito High School in El Cerrito, Calif. (Google Street View) El Cerrito police said Thursday they expect to make "multiple arrests" following an investigation into two years of alleged hazing in the city's high school football program. The El Cerrito Police Department said in a news release that it had received a report of alleged bullying and hazing at El Cerrito High School on Oct. 2. Through its subsequent investigation, which included interviews with witnesses and school staff and the discovery of video evidence, the department said it had identified 22 current and former students who are suspected of committing "battery, sexual battery, assault, false imprisonment, dissuading a victim, conspiracy, and stalking." The abuse had occurred between September 2024 and October 2026, the department said in the release. The investigation remains active, and detectives continue to evaluate evidence. In response to the allegations, the West Contra Costa Unified School District suspended the Gauchos football program for the rest of the 2026 season. The school district also said it is conducting its own investigation under Title IX. "No child should ever experience what our students have described," said WCCUSD Superintendent Cheryl Cotton said in a statement. "While we have worked to focus on accountability for the actions of individual players up until this point, new information has led to new decisions. We must now make the very tough call to immediately suspend the El Cerrito High football program in order to prevent any further harm and restore a safe learning environment for our students." El Cerrito police Capt. Lauren Caputo declined to offer further details in a phone call with SFGATE on Thursday morning, saying that because the investigation involved juvenile victims, he was prohibited from discussing the case further. It's the latest in an eventful few years for the El Cerrito football team. In 2024, it forfeited six games for using ineligible players, which ultimately led to head coach Jacob Rincon's ouster. Last year, under new head coach Tim Johnson, the Gauchos won a California International Federation state championship in the sport, going 13-2 and taking home the school's first state title. The Gauchos had gone 6-3 in the 2026 season so far and had their season finale scheduled for Friday night at De Anza High School in El Sobrante before the start of the North Coast Section playoffs next week. top.title: Former Angels GM Perry Minasian returns to the Braves organization, per report
top.description: Anaheim, CA - November 15: Angeles general manager Perry Minasian listens to a reporter's question after introducing Angels new manager Ron Washington during his introduction news conference at Angel Stadium in Anaheim Wednesday, Nov. 15, 2023. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) That sound you’re hearing blasting from Cobb County right now is the front office for the Atlanta Braves blaring a familiar tune from Thin Lizzy . Not too long ago, former Astros GM Dana Brown returned to the franchise as a senior adviser for amateur scouting. Now, former Angels GM Perry Minasian is returning to the Braves to work with Alex Anthopoulos once again. Bob Nightengale of USA Today was the first to report the news and Jesús Cano of The Athletic added on that Minasian is returning in the same role as Dana Brown, so those two will be working together. There’s not a ton to say here, other than it seems pretty exciting that the Braves are bolstering their front office with some proven (and familiar) figures around here. Both of these guys have worked well with Anthopoulos in the past and had success with the Braves as well, so hopefully we’ll be able to see them pick up where they left off in their new roles with Atlanta for the 2027 season. Brown was last season with the Braves in 2022, while Minasian will be returning after leaving following the 2020 season. If I had to guess, both executives were probably willing to take on their jobs as sort of a holding situation for another big job opening up in the future but that’s pure and total speculation on my part. The tangible part here is that their experience and familiarity should be a positive for the organization going forward — especially (as Gaurav Vedak mentions below) considering that the farm is also starting to look encouraging for the first time in a while. Ronit Shah, Dana Brown, and Perry Minasian managing a quickly developing Braves farm system that has two of the top 40 prospects in baseball. We are going to have some FUN in 2027. Let me interview them @Braves — Gaurav (@gvedak) November 6, 2026 So yeah, hopefully we’ll see this front office continue to be competent and get stuff done, as they will surely benefit from now having both Dana Brown and Perry Minasian back in the fold for the moment.

top.title: NEW Lutheran volleyball falls in state semifinal, while Bay Port wins first match
top.description: ASHWAUBENON – The Northeastern Wisconsin Lutheran girls volleyball program waited 19 years to earn a trip back to the WIAA state tournament. It will have to wait at least one more to get its first win on the big stage. NEW Lutheran had its season end in four sets against Central Wisconsin Christian in a WIAA Division 5 semifinal at the Resch Center on Nov. 5, losing 25-22, 21-25, 25-22, 25-20. It was the Blazers’ first loss in a best-of-five format in 2026 and came against the same team that ended their season in a sectional semifinal last year. Senior setter and Lakeland University commit Olivia Kirchner led NEW with a match-high 32 assists, senior outside hitter and Wisconsin Lutheran College commit Kiley Dhein had a team-high 13 kills and senior libero Meredith Lemke-Scott finished with 19 digs. “It was a great match,” said NEW coach Michael Schmidt, who is in his 14th season with the team and has more than 300 career wins. “I knew it was going to be a battle all the way through. We scouted them well. We knew what they were capable of, we knew what we were capable of. “Just having a chance to be here on the floor and lay it all out there, that was really great. Really awesome.” The Blazers trailed the Crusaders after one set, which was just the second set they had lost since regional play started. But it was nothing to panic about. NEW (33-12) dropped the first set to Florence in a sectional championship and responded by winning three straight to punch its ticket to state. It looked like it might happen again. The Blazers broke a 17-all tie in the second set on a kill by Paige Loock and extended the lead after two more kills from Dhein. The Crusaders (31-8) got to within 22-21, but NEW responded by scoring the final four points to even the match at one set. “In a match of five, that first set is so big,” Central Wisconsin Christian coach Dan TenNapel said. “They come back and win set two. That third set, when it’s tied 1-1, that just dictates so much of the match. It takes so much pressure off you, puts so much pressure on the other team.” It was Central Wisconsin Christian that put all the pressure back on NEW. It was cruising in the third set after taking a 19-12 lead, and even after the Blazers roared back to tie the score at 22, the Crusaders won the last three points to close out the set. “I think with how things got toward the end, it is hard to come back,” Schmidt said. “We were battling, battling, battling and then we just had too many errors at really inopportune times. “We had some net touches that didn’t go our way. We had some serves that didn’t go our way. It’s really hard to be successful when we are making errors ourselves.” The Crusaders took a 7-6 lead in the fourth set and never relinquished it, advancing to the title match on Nov. 7 against Turtle Lake. top.title: Green Bay Packers will continue to stick with Trey Smack despite rookie’s recent struggles
top.description: Beyond their running game, the Green Bay Packers must also find consistency in their kicking game if they have plans to become a legitimate Super Bowl contender this season. After letting go of Brandon McManus this summer, they have relied on Trey Smack , whom they traded up to in the sixth round during this year’s NFL Draft. While everyone expected there would be some growing pains with a rookie kicker, those concerns reared their ugly head in Week 8 against the Carolina Panthers, as Smack now leads the league with eight missed kicks (5 FGs, 3 PATs) – the most for a Packers kicker in the first eight games of a season since Max Zendejas had nine in 1988. Trey Smack’s Week 8 performance with the Green Bay Packers Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) watches a field goal miss during the first quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack finished with three points after going 3-for-4 on his PATs. Overall, the Florida product has gone 11-for-16 on field goals (68.8 percent – good for 30th in the league) and 16-for-19 on PATs (84.2 percent – good for 31st in the league) for 49 points this campaign. However, he will be remembered more for his first attempt, when he hit a “doink” off the left upright in the first quarter after Tucker Kraft made it 6-3, which gave Carolina a sliver of hope. Fortunately for Green Bay, his early miss didn’t cost them, as Josh Jacobs and Matthew Golden scored two more touchdowns. Green Bay Packers remain committed to Trey Smack Aug 28, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) during the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images In a recent media availability, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is adamant about sticking with Trey Smack at kicker, despite his recent struggles. That said, Smack has to repay the team’s trust in him in the next few games. “I think he’s done a lot of good things,” LaFleur said of Smack . “The thing I like about Trey is he’s shown to bounce back. Never want to be in a bounce-back situation, but that’s football. You got to be able to be resilient and go out there and play the next play. It started off bad, obviously, this last game missing a PAT, and then he responded.” More Green Bay Packers news from Wisconsin Sports Heroics Green Bay Packers: 3 studs and duds as 2026 NFL season hits halfway point NFL expands investigation into Packers’ Josh Jacobs after three more women make allegations Green Bay Packers: Jordan Love is having an MVP-caliber season despite horrid offensive deficiencies

top.title: Tigers' top prospect won't play in Arizona Fall League All-Star Game
top.description: The Tigers' No. 1-ranked prospect's season is over. Zyhir Hope is finished playing in 2026, after a hectic year in which he was dealt from the Los Angeles Dodgers to the Tigers in the Tarik Skubal trade. He then played in the Arizona Fall League. Hope was named to the Arizona Fall League All-Star Game, which is scheduled for Sunday night. But he won't play in the game. The Tigers decided before sending him to the AFL that his season would end at the end of October. More: Three Tigers among finalists for American League Silver Slugger awards Hope, 21, played 16 games for the Scottsdale Scorpions in the AFL and slashed .241/.405/.293 with one home run and 11 RBIs. He walked 14 times and struck out 16 times. Hope was one of three prospects sent from the Dodgers to the Tigers for Skubal, the two-time Cy Young winner, in early August, along with right-handed pitchers River Ryan and Brady Smith. Hope, a left-handed-hitting outfielder, played 30 regular-season games for Double-A Erie after the trade, with six homers, 24 RBIs and eight stolen bases. Before the trade, he had 23 homers, 87 RBIs and 18 stolen bases for Double-A Tulsa in the Dodgers' organization. For the year at Double A, he slashed .287/.367/.513 with 29 home runs, 111 RBIs and 26 stolen bases (he was caught six times). He had 62 walks and 141 strikeouts in 124 games. More: Kevin McGonigle named Tiger of the Year by Detroit baseball writers Hope was an 11th-round pick by the Chicago Cubs in the 2023 Major League Baseball Draft, and was dealt to the Dodgers in January 2024. He is the No. 26-ranked prospect in baseball, according to MLB Pipeline, and is expected to make his major-league debut with the Tigers at some point in 2027, Tigers president Scott Harris said in late September. Hope likely will start 2027 at Triple-A Toledo. Ryan, the No. 3 Tigers prospect according to MLB Pipeline, made his Tigers debut in September , while Smith, the No. 9 prospect, is father away from the major leagues. He pitched in Single A in 2026. The AFL season ends Friday, with the All-Star Game set for 8 p.m. Sunday at Salt River Fields in Scottsdale. Hope was the only Tigers prospect selected to the American League's All-Star roster. Seven other Tigers participated in the 2026 AFL: Shortstop Bryce Rainer, the Tigers' No. 2-ranked prospect ; infielder John Peck; and pitchers Logan Berrier, Jalen Evans, Preston Howey, Maddox Long and Win Scott. tpaul@detroitnews.com @tonypaul1984 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Tigers' top prospect won't play in Arizona Fall League All-Star Game

top.title: Packers’ Matt LaFleur won’t say too much about Jordan Love’s blind ref costume, but admits it was ‘hilarious’
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Packers’ Matt LaFleur won’t say too much about Jordan Love’s blind ref costume, but admits it was ‘hilarious’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers have the serious business of trying to chase down their three NFC North rivals. It may be the toughest job in the NFL. Jordan Love and his wife were blind referees for Halloween pic.twitter.com/aKp85sVeWA — Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) November 4, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Packers are playing quite well as they have won four of their last five games and own a 5-3 record. However, in the brutal NFC North, that has left them in fourth place in the division. The Packers have a pair of tough games coming up as they face the New England Patriots in Week 9 before hosting the Vikings in Week 10. The Packers have been hit hard by penalty calls in recent weeks, and quarterback Jordan Love and his wife dressed up as blind NFL referees for the recently concluded Halloween celebration. The Halloween costumes were designed as a joke, but NFL officials don’t take kindly to criticism of its officials by players or coaches. If the NFL looks at this as tongue-in-cheek criticism, there could be a rebuke or a fine. Love sent the video of the costumes to Packers head coach Matt LaFleur , and the head coach thought the quarterback’s take was quite funny but didn’t go much further. “He did send me the clip and I thought it was pretty hilarious,” LaFleur said , per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic . “But I should probably refrain from commenting on that.” Love is regularly viewed as one of the most talented quarterbacks in the NFL because of his ability to throw deep passes to his receivers. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for a league-high 2,246 yards. He has a 16-6 TD-interception ratio. top.title: Cardinals' Tyler Allgeier's recent play just hints at his potential
top.description: Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier took charge over the Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 8 but this should only be a point of reference for what General Manager Monti Ossenfort already knew. Allgeier's 11 attempts and 147 rushing yards might may some marvel but it only reinforces the optimism of head coach Mike LaFleur regarding the offense's potential upside. LaFleur wants his offense to play with fuel and fire but most of their offensive possessions have stalled out due to negative plays and sacks allowed by former starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett. With quarterback Gardner Minshew taking over the most important leadership role on offense, the franchise can expect to see more ball distribution and decency overall. Allgeier knows that his ability to get those tough short-yardage gains and wear down opposing defenses late in games makes him an asset to LaFleur and the offense. LaFleur has the personnel to be productive and multi-faceted and the collective offensive output in Week 8 surely showcased that. On Sunday, the Cardinals kept the contest within striking distance and were able to finally feed off of Allgeier's epic 63-yard touchdown run in the final minute of the third quarter. Allgeier's ability to sway the game's momentum and ignite the turnaround is not something the Cardinals will take as a result of luck but rather it speaks to Allgeier's determination and outright preparation. As a tandem, Allgeier and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love could play as a staple for the franchise, and their complementary running styles create a duality that is needed for the team. Ultimately, Allgeier's services will be needed for the Cardinals to continue running a balanced offensive attack. The team's 33-point output in Week 8 wouldn't have come to pass if not for Allgeier. top.title: Devin Haney-Liam Paro welterweight unification official for Dec. 19 at Chase Center
top.description: Devin Haney drops Brian Norman Jr. on his way to winning the WBO welterweight title in November 2025. SAN FRANCISCO — Devin Haney’s homecoming has a date. The three-division champion and WBO welterweight titleholder will face IBF champion Liam Paro in a welterweight unification fight Saturday, Dec. 19, at Chase Center, Top Rank announced Thursday. The card will stream live on DAZN PPV beginning at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. It is promoted by Top Rank and Devin Haney Promotions, in association with No Limit Boxing and TGB Promotions, and it marks Haney’s first fight under his new DAZN deal. Ticket information will be announced soon. Haney (33-0, 15 KOs) won the WBO welterweight title in November 2025, dropping Brian Norman Jr. on his way to a unanimous decision. Dec. 19 will be his second appearance at Chase Center, where he stopped the clock on Regis Prograis in December 2023 to become a two-division champion at 140 pounds. Now he looks to unify titles in a second weight class. Paro (28-1, 16 KOs), a native of Mackay, Australia, became a two-division world champion in June when he handed Lewis Crocker his first defeat by unanimous decision in Brisbane. He has made a habit of winning away from home. In June 2024, he outpointed Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico to capture the super lightweight world title. “My resume speaks for itself. I’ve never been afraid to go into a champion’s backyard and put my record on the line,” Haney said. “I went to Australia, took George Kambosos’ belts, and became undisputed lightweight champion of the world. Now I’m bringing another Australian world champion, Liam Paro, into my backyard. This time, I plan to take his belt and become a unified welterweight world champion right here at home.” Paro said he saw this one coming. “Three years ago, I was on the undercard at Chase Center the night Devin fought Regis Prograis. I said back then that Haney versus Paro rolls off the tongue. Now it’s here,” he said. “I’ve been the underdog plenty of times and I’ve made history before. December 19, I’m coming to unify the division and make more history.” Bill Haney, whose Devin Haney Promotions is co-promoting the event, said the group is looking to build on its earlier Bay Area success. “We made championship history at Chase Center at 140 pounds. nigeria.title: Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh
nigeria.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has warned opposition parties against celebrating the court judgment that sacked the David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy. Ameh said the ruling should not be seen as a victory for any political camp, warning that the All Progressives Congress (APC) stood to benefit from divisions within the opposition. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday, urging opposition parties to resist attempts to turn the judgment into an opportunity for political infighting. According to him, the APC would be comfortable with any opposition party being weakened, regardless of the party’s identity or political affiliation. “The APC, which is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment, will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened. They do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said. Ameh cautioned that what might appear to be a victory for one faction today could become a tool against another political group tomorrow. “Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield,” he said. He added: “Stay alert. This is not a win for any side. It is a warning.” The NDC candidate urged opposition parties to channel their energy towards demanding free, fair and credible elections, rather than engaging in disputes over political leadership and candidacies. He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to deliver good governance to Nigerians over the past 11 years. “For 11 years, this APC government has failed to provide good governance to Nigerians. nigeria.description: …Zulum pledges business-friendly reforms By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The United Nations (UN), European Union (EU), German Government and other development partners are supporting efforts to attract private investment to Borno State to create jobs and help displaced families rebuild their livelihoods. At the third Borno State Private Sector Engagement and Investment Roundtable in Abuja on Thursday, representatives of the UN, EU and German Embassy pledged continued support for the state’s recovery through private sector investment. The Governor Babagana Zulum-led administration initiated the roundtable series with a meeting in Lagos, focusing on financing bankable projects and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The second edition was held in Kano, with emphasis on agriculture, livestock, fisheries and infrastructure. More than 50 prospective investors attended the Abuja roundtable. The representative of the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office in Nigeria, Thembekile Dube-Nanbe, urged development partners to translate the investment initiative into concrete action. “Let us identify viable investment opportunities, mobilise capital, establish lasting partnerships, and commit to measurable results,” Dube-Nanbe said. The EU Head of Human Development, Laila Ben Amor Mathieu, said the Union had supported Borno through its most difficult years by providing humanitarian assistance and backing stabilisation and recovery efforts. “Grants and public budgets alone will not finance recovery at the scale Borno needs. Private capital must play its part, and the role of us partners is to make that possible,” Mathieu said. She said investors could support the proposed Borno State Durable Solutions Trust Fund or pursue commercially viable projects backed by incentives, including access to land, industrial hubs and tax measures. Mathieu urged businesses to identify projects for further consideration, partner with local companies and create opportunities for women and young people. “Borno is becoming an investment story. The European Union is proud to be part of it,” she said. nigeria.title: Benue SEMA raises alarm over rising snakebites, treats two IDPs
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) has expressed concern over rising cases of snakebites across the state, warning that the incidents are increasingly affecting farmers, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable residents. The concern followed two recent snakebite incidents involving a 35-year-old man, Isaac Shula, and a 19-year-old girl, Mbapuun Tyoshio, both residents of Daudu 1 IDP camp in Guma Local Government Area of the state. The victims were reportedly bitten by snakes while working on their farms and have since been referred to the Benue State University Teaching Hospital (BSUTH), Makurdi, where they are receiving medical attention under the care of Benue SEMA. The agency’s Health Focal Person, Dr Amos Dzungwe, said snakebite cases had continued to increase across the state, affecting not only displaced persons but also farmers and other vulnerable populations. He said the agency had received numerous requests for medical intervention from different parts of the state, reflecting growing concern over the incidents. According to him, two snakebite patients were successfully discharged within the last two weeks, while others remained on admission and were receiving treatment. Dzungwe warned against delays in seeking medical attention, stressing that late presentation at health facilities could result in severe complications and poor health outcomes. He urged members of the public to seek immediate medical attention at appropriate health facilities whenever snakebite incidents occur. Meanwhile, Benue SEMA has urged the public to disregard what it described as misleading reports and politically motivated narratives surrounding snakebite incidents in the state, particularly those involving IDPs. The agency maintained that health emergencies and the lives of vulnerable citizens should not be subjected to political manipulation. It reaffirmed its commitment to providing timely medical assistance to snakebite victims and others affected by emergencies, irrespective of their status or location. nigeria.title: Soludo seeks partnership with pharmacists to strengthen healthcare
nigeria.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for a strategic partnership between the state government and the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to strengthen the healthcare system and improve access to quality pharmaceutical services. Soludo made the call on Wednesday while declaring open the ongoing four-day 99th Annual National Delegate Conference of the society in Awka, stressing that pharmacists played a critical role in building an effective healthcare system. Describing the gathering, tagged ‘Ijele 2026’, as historic, the governor said his administration had prioritised human capital development, education and healthcare. He cited the introduction of free education from kindergarten to Senior Secondary School Three (SS3), as well as free antenatal care in government hospitals, as part of his administration’s interventions in the sectors. Soludo also said his government had revamped the state’s primary healthcare system, disclosing that more than 250,000 expectant mothers had benefited from zero-cost antenatal care, while over 950 free Caesarean Section operations had been performed. “To further solidify Anambra’s position as the nation’s premier pharma hub, let me also inform you that work on the development of the state-of-the-art Pharmaceutical Hub in Oba, alongside the upcoming Coordinated Wholesale Centre slated for delivery early next year, is currently ongoing in the state,” he said. The governor urged the PSN leadership to work closely with the state government to enforce safety standards in pharmaceutical operations and tackle the circulation of counterfeit drugs. He also challenged the society to address unethical practices within the profession, particularly the activities of illegal drug outlets operating under the guise of licensed pharmacies. Earlier, the President of the PSN, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, expressed appreciation to Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession and the decision to host the society’s flagship national conference in Anambra. nigeria.title: Poor financial records, cash flow woes crippling Nigerian businesses — SWAN
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Society of Women Accountants of Nigeria (SWAN) has identified poor financial record-keeping, inadequate cash flow management, ineffective pricing and limited understanding of profitability as some of the factors undermining the survival and growth of businesses in Nigeria. The association said many promising businesses struggle not necessarily because of a lack of opportunities or customers, but because their owners lack the financial knowledge required to manage resources and make informed decisions. SWAN stated this at its 2026 Accounting for Non-Accountants Workshop, held on Thursday at the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) Annex, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. The workshop, organised as part of the association’s Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives, had the theme, “Business Made Easy: Practical Financial Skills.” Speaking at the event, Chairperson of the Planning Committee, Mrs Ruth Jawo, said financial literacy had become essential for entrepreneurs, traders, professionals, employees and business managers, particularly amid the country’s challenging economic conditions. According to her, financial knowledge would enable business owners to make informed decisions, manage resources effectively, avoid penalties and achieve sustainable growth. “The theme reflects SWAN’s commitment to simplifying financial concepts and equipping participants with practical knowledge,” she said. Jawo explained that the workshop was designed to bridge existing financial knowledge gaps and empower participants to manage their finances more confidently. She expressed the expectation that participants would apply the knowledge acquired to improve their businesses, workplaces and households. “Our expectation is that every participant leaves with valuable knowledge, practical tools and a renewed determination to develop better financial habits. “The true success of this workshop will be measured not merely by attendance, but by the positive changes it inspires in businesses, workplaces and households,” she said. nigeria.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League as Milan lose again
nigeria.description: Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches. Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty. Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes. Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth’s substitutes sent the European newcomers top of the table with a fourth successive victory. Marco Rose’s side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend. “It’s a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp,” Rose told TNT Sports. “It’s up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble.” Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe. Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off. “We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight,” Amorim told Sky Sport. “I don’t want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance.” Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase. “I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting,” Amorim added. Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage’s struggling side. nigeria.title: Ebola patient flown to UK from DR Congo
nigeria.description: A UK medic who tested positive for Ebola while working on the outbreak of the disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown to London for treatment, the government said Thursday. The unnamed British citizen “has returned to the UK for specialist treatment after testing positive for the disease”, the government said in a statement. Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. The British government said that the UK medic is now being treated at the Royal Free Hospital in London. This hospital has a high-level isolation unit “specifically designed for this purpose” and strict protocols to prevent contact with the general public, it said. Renu Bindra, deputy director of the all hazards public health response team at the UK health security agency (UKHSA) said “the risk to the wider public remains low”. nigeria.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” Oshiomhole said. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. He said technology would make it easier for security agencies to establish people’s identities and track criminal activities. He disclosed that the Federal Government allocated ₦5.4 trillion to defence in the 2026 budget and was recruiting an additional 12,000 military personnel to strengthen manpower and security coverage. nigeria.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
nigeria.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Greek analyses of the text say that once net gains clear that ceiling, the 10% rate applies to the full net gain for the year, not only the slice above €500. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. sports.title: El Cerrito police expect to make 'multiple arrests' over HS football hazing
sports.description: El Cerrito High School in El Cerrito, Calif. (Google Street View) El Cerrito police said Thursday they expect to make "multiple arrests" following an investigation into two years of alleged hazing in the city's high school football program. The El Cerrito Police Department said in a news release that it had received a report of alleged bullying and hazing at El Cerrito High School on Oct. 2. Through its subsequent investigation, which included interviews with witnesses and school staff and the discovery of video evidence, the department said it had identified 22 current and former students who are suspected of committing "battery, sexual battery, assault, false imprisonment, dissuading a victim, conspiracy, and stalking." The abuse had occurred between September 2024 and October 2026, the department said in the release. The investigation remains active, and detectives continue to evaluate evidence. In response to the allegations, the West Contra Costa Unified School District suspended the Gauchos football program for the rest of the 2026 season. The school district also said it is conducting its own investigation under Title IX. "No child should ever experience what our students have described," said WCCUSD Superintendent Cheryl Cotton said in a statement. "While we have worked to focus on accountability for the actions of individual players up until this point, new information has led to new decisions. We must now make the very tough call to immediately suspend the El Cerrito High football program in order to prevent any further harm and restore a safe learning environment for our students." El Cerrito police Capt. Lauren Caputo declined to offer further details in a phone call with SFGATE on Thursday morning, saying that because the investigation involved juvenile victims, he was prohibited from discussing the case further. It's the latest in an eventful few years for the El Cerrito football team. In 2024, it forfeited six games for using ineligible players, which ultimately led to head coach Jacob Rincon's ouster. Last year, under new head coach Tim Johnson, the Gauchos won a California International Federation state championship in the sport, going 13-2 and taking home the school's first state title. The Gauchos had gone 6-3 in the 2026 season so far and had their season finale scheduled for Friday night at De Anza High School in El Sobrante before the start of the North Coast Section playoffs next week. sports.description: ASHWAUBENON – The Northeastern Wisconsin Lutheran girls volleyball program waited 19 years to earn a trip back to the WIAA state tournament. It will have to wait at least one more to get its first win on the big stage. NEW Lutheran had its season end in four sets against Central Wisconsin Christian in a WIAA Division 5 semifinal at the Resch Center on Nov. 5, losing 25-22, 21-25, 25-22, 25-20. It was the Blazers’ first loss in a best-of-five format in 2026 and came against the same team that ended their season in a sectional semifinal last year. Senior setter and Lakeland University commit Olivia Kirchner led NEW with a match-high 32 assists, senior outside hitter and Wisconsin Lutheran College commit Kiley Dhein had a team-high 13 kills and senior libero Meredith Lemke-Scott finished with 19 digs. “It was a great match,” said NEW coach Michael Schmidt, who is in his 14th season with the team and has more than 300 career wins. “I knew it was going to be a battle all the way through. We scouted them well. We knew what they were capable of, we knew what we were capable of. “Just having a chance to be here on the floor and lay it all out there, that was really great. Really awesome.” The Blazers trailed the Crusaders after one set, which was just the second set they had lost since regional play started. But it was nothing to panic about. NEW (33-12) dropped the first set to Florence in a sectional championship and responded by winning three straight to punch its ticket to state. It looked like it might happen again. The Blazers broke a 17-all tie in the second set on a kill by Paige Loock and extended the lead after two more kills from Dhein. sports.title: Tigers' top prospect won't play in Arizona Fall League All-Star Game
sports.description: The Tigers' No. 1-ranked prospect's season is over. Zyhir Hope is finished playing in 2026, after a hectic year in which he was dealt from the Los Angeles Dodgers to the Tigers in the Tarik Skubal trade. He then played in the Arizona Fall League. Hope was named to the Arizona Fall League All-Star Game, which is scheduled for Sunday night. But he won't play in the game. The Tigers decided before sending him to the AFL that his season would end at the end of October. More: Three Tigers among finalists for American League Silver Slugger awards Hope, 21, played 16 games for the Scottsdale Scorpions in the AFL and slashed .241/.405/.293 with one home run and 11 RBIs. He walked 14 times and struck out 16 times. Hope was one of three prospects sent from the Dodgers to the Tigers for Skubal, the two-time Cy Young winner, in early August, along with right-handed pitchers River Ryan and Brady Smith. Hope, a left-handed-hitting outfielder, played 30 regular-season games for Double-A Erie after the trade, with six homers, 24 RBIs and eight stolen bases. Before the trade, he had 23 homers, 87 RBIs and 18 stolen bases for Double-A Tulsa in the Dodgers' organization. For the year at Double A, he slashed .287/.367/.513 with 29 home runs, 111 RBIs and 26 stolen bases (he was caught six times). He had 62 walks and 141 strikeouts in 124 games. More: Kevin McGonigle named Tiger of the Year by Detroit baseball writers Hope was an 11th-round pick by the Chicago Cubs in the 2023 Major League Baseball Draft, and was dealt to the Dodgers in January 2024. He is the No. 26-ranked prospect in baseball, according to MLB Pipeline, and is expected to make his major-league debut with the Tigers at some point in 2027, Tigers president Scott Harris said in late September. Hope likely will start 2027 at Triple-A Toledo. Ryan, the No. 3 Tigers prospect according to MLB Pipeline, made his Tigers debut in September , while Smith, the No. 9 prospect, is father away from the major leagues. He pitched in Single A in 2026. The AFL season ends Friday, with the All-Star Game set for 8 p.m. Sunday at Salt River Fields in Scottsdale. Hope was the only Tigers prospect selected to the American League's All-Star roster. sports.title: Cardinals' Tyler Allgeier's recent play just hints at his potential
sports.description: Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier took charge over the Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 8 but this should only be a point of reference for what General Manager Monti Ossenfort already knew. Allgeier's 11 attempts and 147 rushing yards might may some marvel but it only reinforces the optimism of head coach Mike LaFleur regarding the offense's potential upside. LaFleur wants his offense to play with fuel and fire but most of their offensive possessions have stalled out due to negative plays and sacks allowed by former starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett. With quarterback Gardner Minshew taking over the most important leadership role on offense, the franchise can expect to see more ball distribution and decency overall. Allgeier knows that his ability to get those tough short-yardage gains and wear down opposing defenses late in games makes him an asset to LaFleur and the offense. LaFleur has the personnel to be productive and multi-faceted and the collective offensive output in Week 8 surely showcased that. On Sunday, the Cardinals kept the contest within striking distance and were able to finally feed off of Allgeier's epic 63-yard touchdown run in the final minute of the third quarter. Allgeier's ability to sway the game's momentum and ignite the turnaround is not something the Cardinals will take as a result of luck but rather it speaks to Allgeier's determination and outright preparation. As a tandem, Allgeier and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love could play as a staple for the franchise, and their complementary running styles create a duality that is needed for the team. Ultimately, Allgeier's services will be needed for the Cardinals to continue running a balanced offensive attack. The team's 33-point output in Week 8 wouldn't have come to pass if not for Allgeier. sports.title: Devin Haney-Liam Paro welterweight unification official for Dec. 19 at Chase Center
sports.description: Devin Haney drops Brian Norman Jr. on his way to winning the WBO welterweight title in November 2025. SAN FRANCISCO — Devin Haney’s homecoming has a date. The three-division champion and WBO welterweight titleholder will face IBF champion Liam Paro in a welterweight unification fight Saturday, Dec. 19, at Chase Center, Top Rank announced Thursday. The card will stream live on DAZN PPV beginning at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. It is promoted by Top Rank and Devin Haney Promotions, in association with No Limit Boxing and TGB Promotions, and it marks Haney’s first fight under his new DAZN deal. Ticket information will be announced soon. Haney (33-0, 15 KOs) won the WBO welterweight title in November 2025, dropping Brian Norman Jr. on his way to a unanimous decision. Dec. 19 will be his second appearance at Chase Center, where he stopped the clock on Regis Prograis in December 2023 to become a two-division champion at 140 pounds. Now he looks to unify titles in a second weight class. Paro (28-1, 16 KOs), a native of Mackay, Australia, became a two-division world champion in June when he handed Lewis Crocker his first defeat by unanimous decision in Brisbane. He has made a habit of winning away from home. In June 2024, he outpointed Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico to capture the super lightweight world title. “My resume speaks for itself. technology.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
technology.description: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations. One connection, works every time, needs no retries There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts. Read full article Comments

Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing. The gist of the new policy, according to Google's blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts. When Google revealed its new policy, the company's VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times , which interpreted the situation as Google will "turn off search" if schools reject AI. This has a nefarious vibe, but it's probably not the most accurate way to describe how Google's educational AI system will operate. technology.title: The White House is apparently a popular residential proxy exit spot
technology.description: Whether through malware or other means, devices associated with the White House network appear to be serving as residential proxy exit nodes, potentially posing security risks to one of the world's most sensitive networks. News of the security snafu comes from security firm Layer3 Intel, which reported this week that it discovered the likely illicit activity thanks to its recently launched Residential Proxy Observatory . According to Layer3 founder Sergiy Usatyuk, the White House residential proxy activity might have gone unnoticed if not for the new tool. “The observatory is just a public interface to explore the data we've been collecting for the past year,” Usatyuk told The Register in an email. For those unfamiliar with residential proxies, they're like any old proxy network that obfuscates the location of a user, except in this case their exit nodes use IP addresses associated with residential internet connections, as opposed to datacenters. While many are legitimate, others are exploited by threat actors and used in the commission of cybercrimes, as the FBI warned earlier this year. The FBI bulletin, put out in March, warns users to protect their systems against hijacking via malware, illicit SDK partnerships, VPNs with hidden service terms that repurpose user computers as exit nodes, and other threats used to turn victims into nodes without their consent. Residential proxies are commonly used by threat actors to conceal command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, conduct phishing attacks, send spam, disguise malicious traffic, and the like, the FBI explained. According to Layer3, its data shows 28 distinct residential proxy services exiting into the White House network nearly every day between October 5 and November 3, with 236 separate exits in that period. Other residential proxy detection services logged the same information, Layer3 said. Most of the activity was happening in the evening, White House time, between 5 pm and midnight. That, Layer3 said, suggests someone at the White House - not a guest - has an infected device that’s serving as an exit, likely via an infected proxy SDK. If correct, that’s a problem. “Past research has shown that poorly secured proxy SDKs can allow internal network access and lateral movement,” Layer3 explained. “If an SDK on this network has the same kind of flaw, anyone buying proxy access could use it to reach internal systems.” In other words, this is a serious security risk, and one Usatyuk tells us could have been a problem for a while. “Our data retention period goes back to July 10,” the Layer3 founder explained. “Given that there was continuous activity for a matter of months and other res proxy detection services independently verified the data, it's likely that White House IPs have been used by res proxy networks for all sorts of activity for some time now.” Usatyuk said his firm’s data isn’t detailed enough to know how many machines are being used as exit nodes inside the White House network. technology.title: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
technology.description: With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are eager to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet. While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star's light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope's configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets. Point spreads Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function. Read full article Comments

science.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
science.description: null Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon (at far right) is seen at the base of the newly-deployed eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit. Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem. "We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy." To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment. Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue. "We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell. Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk (at center) works on mounting the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes. "Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. Half the size of the old ones and bringing 40% more power." NASA graphic showing the location and power channel

Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. science.title: The economic benefits of the covid vaccines may be double what we thought
science.description: The covid-19 vaccines were costly to produce, but paid for themselves many times over Paul Christian Gordon / Alamy The covid-19 vaccines may have provided health and economic benefits worth up to $64.3 trillion in the first year alone – almost double an earlier estimate. Previously, researchers calculated that the $79.4 billion invested in developing covid-19 vaccines saw a return of between $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion globally in the first 12 months after their rollout. But now, a reanalysis of the data suggests it is actually between $6.43 trillion and $64.3 trillion. This means that for every $1 spent on the vaccines’ development, between $59.70 and $809 was gained in that year. “It is great to finally see this research published to demonstrate the enormous health and financial benefits gained from covid-19 vaccines, in comparison to the costs that went into their development and delivery,” says Hallie Benjamin at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. Read more Does each new covid-19 variant pose a significant threat? The $6.43 trillion figure is based on a cost-effectiveness analysis that is generally used in the health sector and factors in quality of life, while the $64.3 trillion figure is based on a cost-benefit analysis used in the public sector. Advertisement Both include data from 173 countries on averted hospitalisations, productivity losses and lives saved. For instance, one of the estimates Benjamin and her colleagues used came from modelling that suggested the vaccines prevented 14 million to 20 million deaths in their first year. The initial $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion figures were released when the research was in a preprint stage, before it had been peer-reviewed. “We made many changes throughout the peer-review process that strengthened the quality of our findings,” says Benjamin. The researchers originally used the Value of Statistical Life Years, which considers how many years a person would be likely to live because of the vaccine, a figure that would be lower if someone was older. As part of the peer-review process, they were advised to use the Value of Statistical Life. Team member Mark Jit at New York University says this treats life spans more equally and is aligned with recommendations for valuing mortality-risk reductions. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter The cost-benefit analysis figure also increased significantly due to a change from calculating the economic value of avoiding a death, says Jit. But the returns weren’t equally distributed. The researchers found that the vaccines had the highest returns in richer countries. This was probably because poorer countries accessed them later, so fewer lives were saved and fewer productivity and healthcare costs were averted, says Jit. The results are “a message about the need for being able to distribute the vaccines fairly to the people most in need around the world”, he says. Covid raises risk of heart issues in children

But the history of such use is likely to go back much further. Genomic studies suggest that the domestication of cannabis plants ( Cannabis sativa ) was happening in China about 12,000 years ago , with people potentially exploiting it for oil and hemp fibre. Archaeological sites with artefacts made from hemp dating to 7500 years ago have been found in China and Japan . The earliest firm evidence of the plant’s use as a drug had been chemical traces on wooden braziers in China that implied humans were “smoking” cannabis 2500 years ago as part of funeral rites. In an excavation trench at the centre of the mound, Caspari and his colleagues recovered almost 1000 whole cannabis seeds.
